title: Native onboarding and first-session journey audit
capture_method: static evidence audit of native client/server sources, tests, and rebuild docs on the routed base; read-only resource capsule (no ports opened, no play-server mutation, no runtime captures)
journey_mode: remote owner path (verdigris_client --remote, chronicles front door default per native/client/main.cpp:4618-4623); local testbed and --quick guest noted where they diverge
design_guards: preserve loose quest guidance: the objective-strip pattern (native/client/main.cpp:2914-2943) is the reference style
no checklist tutorial design: fixes below surface decisions and consequences, they do not add step-list onboarding
all narrative wording, names, and lore stay owner-owned (SPEC owner_input_dependency); fixes are structural only

steps.title: Launch the native client
client_shows: Owner one-command launch: play-native.ps1 builds if stale, starts verdigris_server in the 6520-6539 capsule, and starts the client with --remote (native/tools/play-native.ps1:392-402; native/README.md:40-57)
Default remote mode opens at the Chronicles front door, window title 'Verdigris Chronicles' (native/client/main.cpp:4529-4558, 4618-4623)
No-argument launch instead opens the 'Verdigris Core Testbed' straight into a seeded local simulation as fixed 'House Verdigris' (native/client/main.cpp:4626-4646)
steps.player_decision: Run the owner launcher (or shortcut) rather than the bare exe
evidence: native/README.md:53-57 — desktop shortcut target documented
native/tools/play-native.ps1:40-47 — port 6500 refused; capsule 6520-6539 enforced
native/client/main.cpp:4595-4625 — arg parsing: --headless, --scenario, --reference-scene, --remote
friction: Two different first-session shapes exist: bare exe = anonymous local testbed with a hardcoded House; launcher = Chronicles owner path. A new owner double-clicking an installed exe gets the testbed, not the front door
Local testbed identity is always 'House Verdigris' regardless of any owner account (native/client/main.cpp:4628)
steps.smallest_fix: Make the owner path the no-argument default on Windows (or make the bare exe print/launch the owner path); keep --headless/--scenario/--quick as explicit flags. No wording changes required.

steps.title: Connect to the server; front door opens
client_shows: Status line cycles: 'The chronicles lie closed - connection lost.' (disconnected), 'Opening the chronicles...' (awaiting payload), 'Account of <name>' once chronicles:state arrives (native/client/main.cpp:2483-2495)
Connection chip on every screen: 'connection <state>' with color-coded Ready/Connecting/Retrying/Disconnected (native/client/main.cpp:2570-2616)
Login sends guestId + awaitChronicles:true and the server answers chronicles:state (native/client/remote_session.cpp:277-297; native/src/networking.cpp:2656-2673)
steps.player_decision: Wait for the chronicle payload; nothing else is actionable yet
evidence: native/client/remote_session.cpp:650-671 — chronicles:state/player:chronicles:ready set chronicle.present and chronicles_pending
native/tests/session_tests.cpp:1-5 — dead endpoint is a visible hard failure, never a silent local fallback
friction: No spinner/progress affordance beyond the text line; acceptable at current scope
steps.smallest_fix: None required for legibility; the status line already names the three states.

steps.title: Found the House and name the first Scion
client_shows: Menu rebuilt from the authoritative chronicle model each frame: '[F] Found your House' when no House exists; then numbered '[1..9] Set out as <scion>', '[C] Name a new Scion (<derived name>)', '[M] Mortal oath: not taken/ARMED' (native/client/main.cpp:2321-2369, 2532-2542)
House and Scion names are auto-derived: 'House of <account>' and '<House> Firstborn/Secondborn/...' ordinals (native/client/main.cpp:2292-2317)
Oath field line explains soft vs mortal: 'soft - wounds can be recovered' / 'mortal - death is final' (native/client/main.cpp:2538-2542)
steps.player_decision: Found the House (F), create the Scion (C), optionally arm the mortal oath (M), then set out (digit or Enter)
evidence: native/client/main.cpp:2407-2426 — found/create/select/set-out submit the frozen Gate-B envelopes
native/client/remote_session.cpp:443-484 — chronicles:house:found, chronicles:scion:create, player:chronicles:select (mortal flag), chronicles:scion:set-out
orchestration/tasks/TASK-0145-native-chronicles-owner-journey/REVIEW.md:22 — chronicles-gate-b scenario 38/38 checks accepted
friction: No text input exists anywhere: House and Scion names are derived from the guest identity (comment at native/client/main.cpp:2292-2293 says so explicitly). The owner cannot name their own lineage on the first session
Front door is keyboard-only; the menu lines do show '[key] label', so the input model is at least visible
The mortal-oath consequence line is good, but nothing explains that the oath choice applies to the NEXT admission until you read the label change
steps.smallest_fix: Add a minimal text-input seam (one-line prompt on the front door) for House and Scion names, falling back to the current derived names when left empty. Wording stays owner-owned; this is interaction, not lore.

steps.title: Learn the controls
client_shows: Quickbar with four labeled slots: LMB Strike, Q Thrust, E Sweep, R WarCry (native/client/main.cpp:2124-2129, 2131-2203)
Gear pane footer: 'Arrows select | Enter equip | U unequip | I close' (native/client/main.cpp:2057); empty-backpack hint: 'Backpack empty. X picks up the nearest drop.' (native/client/main.cpp:2015)
Objective strip references 'press F there' for extraction (native/client/main.cpp:2933)
Full control legend (WASD, mouse aim, RMB/Space dash, X, Z, F, I, wheel zoom, Home) exists ONLY inside the F3 debug overlay (native/client/main.cpp:3001-3009)
steps.player_decision: Discover and adopt WASD + mouse + quickbar keys without leaving the fiction
evidence: docs/product/VERDIGRIS_CONSTITUTION.md:94-101 — control reference: WASD, mouse aim, LMB/RMB, Q/E/R, Space, Z loot filter, X pickup, gold auto-pickup
native/client/main.cpp:3167-3246 — implemented bindings match the constitution (W/A/S/D, Space dash, Q/E/R, X, Z, F, I, 1-9, F3, Esc, Home)
friction: The complete key legend is debug-gated (F3); a first-session owner never sees dash (Space/RMB), loot labels (Z), gear (I), or zoom (wheel/Home) documented in-game
native/README.md:36-38 still documents the old bindings ('P picks up, E equips, and X extracts'), contradicting the shipped client — doc drift that misleads anyone reading the README before playing
steps.smallest_fix: Promote a compact always-available controls hint (e.g., one status-chip line or a first-minute fading hint reusing the existing hint system, native/client/main.cpp:812-815) and correct native/README.md:36-38 to the implemented bindings. Loose phrasing, no checklist.

steps.title: Choose an expedition goal
client_shows: Nothing: there is no route, goal, or expedition choice surface on the front door or in the expedition HUD
The only zone entry in the client is a hardcoded 'N' key that enters tin:1:0 (native/client/main.cpp:3189-3190); 'N' is not listed even in the F3 help text (native/client/main.cpp:3001-3009)

The simulation internally tracks expedition phases SlayWardens -> ExtractCarriedValue and emits ExpeditionPhaseChanged (native/include/verdigris/core.hpp:251,301; native/src/core.cpp:850-859), but event_label() has no case for it (native/client/main.cpp:1673-1694) and the objective strip only ever says 'objective: explore the route' or 'objective: reach/carry to the EXIT' (native/client/main.cpp:2917-2943)
steps.player_decision: Pick a specific expedition goal (trophy, material, route) before setting out
evidence: docs/product/VERDIGRIS_CONSTITUTION.md:22-35 — the durable loop begins with 'choose a specific expedition goal'; players leave with a concrete goal, not a checklist quest
native/client/main.cpp:3189-3190 — hardcoded enter_zone('tin:1:0') is the only route choice
native/client/main.cpp:2465-2568 — front door lists House/Scion/oath actions only; no expedition choices
native/client/main.cpp:1673-1694 — ExpeditionPhaseChanged is dropped from the owner-facing event log
friction: This is the audit's negative control: the loop's first player decision (goal choice) is currently invisible. The world auto-assigns tin:1:0 on admission and the objective strip fills in after the fact
The core's own slay-wardens/extract-value phase signal never reaches the HUD, so even the implicit goal of the current route is unexplained
steps.smallest_fix: Two structural, non-lore moves: (1) render the existing ExpeditionPhaseChanged event in the objective strip / event log (label wording owner-owned), and (2) reserve a front-door 'set out toward <route/goal>' choice listing authoritative unlocked routes once more than one exists. No tutorial, no invented copy.

steps.title: First engagement: move, aim, strike, dodge
client_shows: WASD movement with mouse-aim facing; facing line drawn from the Scion (native/client/main.cpp:2756-2764, 3110-3131)

Elite windups drawn as ground telegraphs (thrust fan / sweep circle) with pulse and HUD-safe clipping (native/client/main.cpp:1433-1546); '! <ACTION>' text over the monster bar (native/client/main.cpp:2837-2849)
Impact flash, floating damage numbers (red when the Scion is hit), screen-edge pulse on player damage, death ring/dust on kills (native/client/main.cpp:1774-1813, 1633-1669)
Blocked movement shows hint 'Blocked by scenery' (native/client/main.cpp:3122-3127)
steps.player_decision: Engage or avoid; dodge telegraphed elite attacks (dash with Space/RMB)
evidence: native/client/main.cpp:3535-3551 — scenario first-fight proves swing/damage/death/drop render through the real pipeline
native/client/main.cpp:3633-3663 — scenario telegraph-dodge proves moving out avoids telegraphed damage
native/client/main.cpp:3665-3713 — scenario combat-juice proves target flash, number lifetime, and player-damage pulse
friction: Dash (Space/RMB) is the key defensive answer to telegraphs but is only documented in the F3 overlay (see step 4)
steps.smallest_fix: Same as step 4: surface the compact control hint; optionally name the dash in the telegraph hint path (wording owner-owned).

steps.title: See and take loot
client_shows: Drops render as colored diamonds (gold item, purple trophy) with sparkles at the kill site; Z toggles name labels (native/client/main.cpp:2853-2885, 1823-1841, 3205-3208)

X picks up the nearest drop locally (deterministic nearest scan, native/client/main.cpp:856-886); on the remote path X sends player:take:underfoot and hints 'Take underfoot requested' (native/client/main.cpp:3191-3204; native/client/remote_session.cpp:424-426)
Event log lines 'Picked up <name>' (native/client/presentation_state.cpp:256-258)
steps.player_decision: Walk to drops and spend X (or walk over and take underfoot remotely)
evidence: native/client/main.cpp:3562-3570 — loot-to-bank scenario proves drop visibility and pickup fill the carried grid
docs/product/VERDIGRIS_CONSTITUTION.md:96-97 — X picks up nearest, gold auto-picks up; implemented behavior matches
friction: Remote kill drops are synthesized client-side as 'kill reward' placeholders until a pickup names the item, because the native server drops loot in-world without a ground envelope (native/client/remote_session.cpp:799-806). Labels (Z) show the placeholder, not the real item name
steps.smallest_fix: Client-side only: keep the sparkle but hide the placeholder label until the authoritative name arrives (or label it generically without fake specificity). Server envelope work belongs to a server lane, not this fix.

steps.title: Equip and read gear
client_shows: I opens the Gear/House pane: authoritative stat readout LIFE/RES/ATK (base + equipped bonus)/DEF/LVL, weapon seat, 4-column backpack grid with [E] equipped markers, banked items/trophies footer (native/client/main.cpp:1924-2059)
Digits 1-9 quick-equip carried items; Enter equips the selected cell; U unequips (local) (native/client/main.cpp:3220-3242, 888-896)
Empty-gear attempt hints 'Gear empty: pick up an item first' (native/client/main.cpp:889-892)
steps.player_decision: Compare the equipped bonus and choose what to equip
evidence: native/client/main.cpp:3574-3591 — loot-to-bank scenario proves weapon seat fills and the stat readout shows the (+N) bonus
native/client/presentation_state.cpp:122-132 — remote inventory/equipped sync into the same pane
friction: Only attack bonuses are shown per item; defense/resource/health bonuses parsed from the protocol (native/client/remote_session.cpp:74-93) are not surfaced in the pane, so equip choices under-inform
Remote unequip has no wire command; U silently does nothing off-local (native/client/main.cpp:3232-3235 gates on state->simulation)
steps.smallest_fix: Surface the already-parsed bonuses in the pane rows and disable/hide the U affordance on the remote path (or hint that it is local-only).

steps.title: Extract value to the House
client_shows: EXIT pad: bright pulsing plate with gold chevrons and an 'EXIT' label; minimap shows a gold dot for it (native/client/main.cpp:2636-2684, 2245-2249)
Objective strip points at the EXIT with compass direction and distance, switching to 'carry your loot to the EXIT' while carrying (native/client/main.cpp:2917-2943)

Remote extraction is by walking onto stairs-up; F instead hints 'Reach the exit stairs to return to the surface.' (native/client/remote_session.cpp:437-442); success message 'Returned to the surface' (native/client/presentation_state.cpp:225-228)
steps.player_decision: Push farther or return and bank
evidence: native/client/main.cpp:3605-3629 — loot-to-bank scenario proves extraction banks item+trophy and the objective strip keeps guiding
docs/product/VERDIGRIS_CONSTITUTION.md:48-53 — unextracted value can be lost on death; the return decision is the loop's tension
friction: Contract mismatch on the owner path: the objective strip says 'press F there' (main.cpp:2933) but on remote F does not extract (remote_session.cpp:437-442) — the owner must walk onto the pad. Locally F works. One of the two surfaces is wrong depending on mode
steps.smallest_fix: Make the objective strip mode-aware (remote: point at the pad and say walk-onto; wording owner-owned), or route F to a walk-onto request on remote. Pure interaction contract, no lore.

steps.title: See progression (level, bank, tree)
client_shows: Chronicle roster lists each living Scion with level (and '(mortal)') (native/client/main.cpp:2505-2510); expedition identity chip names House and Scion (native/client/main.cpp:2945-2955)
Gear pane shows LVL plus stats; banked items/trophies counted after extraction (native/client/main.cpp:1968-1979, 2051-2056)
Server derives level from combat XP (native/src/networking.cpp:2045-2052, 1169-1181) and includes a passiveTree object in payloads (native/src/networking.cpp:586, 817)
steps.player_decision: Invest progression (passive tree) — currently impossible in the native client
evidence: native/client/remote_session.cpp:614-917 — apply_envelope handles login/chronicle/combat/state/inventory but never reads passiveTree
grep of native/client: no passiveTree reference in any client file; the payload field is dropped on the floor
docs/product/VERDIGRIS_CONSTITUTION.md:103-106 — player-facing progression includes inventory, stats, a passive skill tree, and loose quest threads
friction: Level-ups happen server-side with no client moment (no flash, no delta line); the number in the pane simply changes
The passive tree exists in the wire contract and server but has no native surface; progression beyond gear is invisible on the first session
steps.smallest_fix: Non-lore minimum: announce level changes (compare model level across dev:state polls and emit the existing hint/event-log line) and add a read-only passive-tree summary chip (points available/spent from the authoritative payload). Full tree UI is a successor lane; this makes progression legible without inventing rules.

steps.title: Understand death and recovery
client_shows: Soft death (lifecycle awaiting-respawn) keeps the expedition screen; hard mortal fall emits chronicles:scion-fallen with the message 'The chronicle records the fall of <name>.' and returns the owner to the front door (native/client/main.cpp:2371-2384; native/client/remote_session.cpp:673-694)

Front door then records the fall with name and level, lists the Scion in the crypt with heirloom status, and offers '[C] Name a new Scion' plus heir-admission ('Set out as <heir>, heir of <fallen>') (native/client/main.cpp:2511-2530, 2329-2356)
Heirloom recovery surfaces the relic in-world and toasts 'Heirloom of <name> recovered' (native/client/main.cpp:2386-2405, 2957-2966)
steps.player_decision: Admit an heir (select path) and understand what was lost/kept
evidence: native/client/main.cpp:2329-2343 — wire contract comment: heirs are admitted through player:chronicles:select (resets permadead lifecycle); set-out is the living scion's road-purse outing

native/client/main.cpp:4049-4108 — gate-b scenario proves fall recording, crypt entry, succession select, and the RECORDED RED: successor inherits a zero-life actor until a fresh heal (routed to TASK-0148, not client-fixable)
native/persistence/README.md:21-28 — snapshot boundary retires the active instance; carried value stays on the Scion, floor value disappears, relic candidates return to recovery queues
friction: The zero-life-heir red is recorded and owned by TASK-0148 (server); until it lands, a succession admission can show a dead-in-world heir — the single worst first-impression moment in the current journey
What death does to carried loot is implemented (persistence boundary) but never stated to the owner in-client; the fall message records the Scion, not the loss rule
Soft death (awaiting-respawn) has no visible explanation on the expedition screen; the owner sees orbs at zero and must guess
steps.smallest_fix: Client-side: on awaiting-respawn show the existing hint channel with an owner-owned explanation line; on succession admission, keep the front door visible until model.player.life > 0 (the scenario already waits on exactly this condition, main.cpp:4103-4107). The heal fix itself stays with TASK-0148.

steps.title: Quit and relaunch
client_shows: Esc or window close quits immediately; session shutdown is clean (native/client/main.cpp:3174-3177, 3302-3305; native/client/remote_session.cpp:372-386)
play-native lifecycle selftest proves normal close exits 0 and both processes are reaped (native/tools/play-native.ps1:262-309, 352-357)
Relaunch restores the account roster: chronicles:state re-renders House, living heirs, and crypt (native/client/main.cpp:4143-4166 scenario step 10)
steps.player_decision: Quit now (abandoning the active instance) or extract first
evidence: native/persistence/README.md:24-28 — an active instance is retired at the snapshot boundary; ordinary floor value disappears, carried value stays with the Scion
native/src/networking.cpp:540 — account state (stats, inventory, quests, chronicle) persists across sessions for guests
friction: Esc quits instantly with no confirmation even while carrying unextracted loot; the loss rule for the abandoned instance exists in the persistence contract but is never shown at the quit moment
No 'quit to front door' (soft exit) distinct from 'quit the game'; both are the same instant action
steps.smallest_fix: When carried value exists, make Esc first show a hint/confirm in the existing hint channel naming the stake (wording owner-owned); second Esc quits. No menus, no checklist.

steps.title: Errors and reconnect
client_shows: Connection chip is always visible on both screens with honest states: connecting/connected/ready/retrying/disconnected/rejected/protocol mismatch (native/client/main.cpp:2570-2616; native/client/remote_session.hpp state enum)
Hard failure banner: 'CONNECTION LOST — not playing offline' plus hint pulse (native/client/main.cpp:2609-2615; native/client/presentation_state.cpp:229-233)
Retry policy: only after having been Ready; 3 attempts at 1s/2s/4s backoff, then terminal 'reconnect failed after 3 attempts' (native/client/remote_session.cpp:311-349)

player:session-replaced is terminal: 'session replaced by a newer connection' (native/client/remote_session.cpp:695-700); protocol upgrade failures classify as ProtocolMismatch (native/client/remote_session.cpp:362-368)
steps.player_decision: Recognize the failure and relaunch (there is no in-client retry control)
evidence: native/tests/session_tests.cpp:405-406 — 'replaced: first session is disconnected' contract test
docs/rebuild/NATIVE_CLIENT_PROTOCOL_MATRIX.md:14 — session-replaced row documents the Disconnected/ConnectionLost contract
friction: After the third failed retry the client sits on the front door with a red chip but no 'retry now' affordance; the only recovery is closing the window and relaunching

Retry only ever re-establishes transport; the front door payload refresh depends on the server re-emitting chronicles:state on the new login (works, but the owner sees 'Opening the chronicles...' again with no explanation of what happened)
steps.smallest_fix: Add a keyboard 'R: attempt to reconnect' action to the front door action list when state is Disconnected/Rejected (it already owns the full action-menu machinery, native/client/main.cpp:2321-2443). Structural, no copy invention.

negative_controls: step 5 goal-choice: the durable loop's first decision has no surface at all (hardcoded tin:1:0; phase events dropped)
step 10 progression: passive-tree progression exists on the wire but has no native surface; level-ups are silent
